mainTopic: Whether jumping that brings on bleeding sets a וסת, and the new משנה on when a woman with a fixed וסת must still check herself.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. רבי מאיר says pregnant and nursing women keep the leniency of 'their time is sufficient' even if they keep bleeding. רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון limit it to the first sighting. רב הונא rules that a woman who jumped and saw blood three times sets a וסת. The גמרא concludes that this is a combined וסת of days plus jumps, and רב אשי gives a case to show why. A second version of רב הונא says the same case sets a וסת of days alone. A new משנה teaches that even a woman with a fixed וסת must check herself and use checking cloths, and it lists when she checks. The exceptions are a נדה and a woman in her days of דם טוהר. The גמרא explains why a נדה need not check, even according to רבי יוחנן. It then tests the exception of דם טוהר against the argument between רב and לוי, and לוי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Pregnant and nursing women stay lenient even while bleeding
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends רבי מאיר's view. Even if a pregnant or nursing woman keeps seeing blood, 'her time is sufficient' for the whole pregnancy and the whole nursing period.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if they keep seeing a steady flow of blood, their time is sufficient for all the days of their pregnancy and all the days of their nursing. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the משנה. רבי מאיר says pregnant and nursing women keep the 'time is sufficient' leniency the whole time, even if they bleed again and again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Time is sufficient' (דַּיָּן שְׁעָתָן) means she becomes impure only from the moment she sees blood, not backward in time. רבי מאיר says repeated bleeding does not take this leniency away for the whole pregnancy or nursing period.

keyTerms.meaning: Flowing with blood; seeing blood again and again
It is enough for them: they are impure only from the moment they see, not backward
The days of their pregnancy
The days of their nursing

phrases.english: Even if they keep flowing with blood
phrases.notes: This line continues the משנה's list of pregnant and nursing women, saying they keep the leniency even in this case.

phrases.english: their time is sufficient all the days of their pregnancy
and their time is sufficient all the days of their nursing,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹפְעוֹת דָּם וּבָאוֹת דַּיָּין כׇּל יְמֵי עִיבּוּרָן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, pregnant and nursing women are not impure backward for the entire pregnancy or nursing period, even if they bleed repeatedly.

steps.title: The other תנאים: The leniency covers only the first sighting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון disagree. The leniency applies only to the first sighting. After that she is treated like any other woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say: The leniency of 'their time is sufficient' was said only for the first sighting. At the second sighting she is impure backward for twenty-four hours, or back to her last examination.
steps.whatsHappening: Three תנאים argue with רבי מאיר and limit the leniency to the first time she sees blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a pregnant or nursing woman sees blood a second time, she loses the special leniency. She is impure backward like a regular woman, for the shorter of twenty-four hours or back to her last check.

keyTerms.meaning: The first sighting of blood
A full twenty-four-hour period backward
From one internal examination to the next

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the leniency lasts the whole pregnancy or nursing period. רבי יוסי, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: it covers only the first sighting.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:
They only said 'their time is sufficient'
for the first sighting,
but at the second sighting
she makes things impure going back twenty-four hours
or from examination to examination.
phrases.notes: A פקידה is an internal check a woman does. She is impure back to her last check if that was less than a day before.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the first sighting gets the leniency. From the second sighting on, she is impure backward like any other woman.

steps.title: רב הונא: Jumping and seeing blood three times sets a וסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about blood caused by an outside force. רב הונא says that if a woman jumped and saw blood three times, she has set a וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And if she saw the first sighting…' רב הונא said: If she jumped and saw, jumped and saw, and jumped and saw, she has set a fixed cycle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה's case of bleeding caused by אונס. רב הונא gives a new rule: three times of jumping and then bleeding creates a וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a וסת is a fixed pattern of when a woman's period comes. רב הונא says a repeated outside cause, like jumping, can also create a pattern. The question of what kind of pattern this is comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: She jumped
A fixed pattern for when a woman's period comes
She established or set
An outside cause, not her natural cycle

phrases.english: 'And if she saw the first, etc.'
Rav Huna said:
If she jumped and saw blood,
jumped and saw blood,
jumped and saw blood,
she has set herself a fixed cycle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם רָאֲתָה רִאשׁוֹנָה וְכוּ׳ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three times of jumping and then seeing blood sets a וסת.

steps.title: What kind of cycle did she set? Not one of days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of וסת she set. It cannot be a cycle of days, because on days she did not jump she did not see blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what did she set a cycle? If you say for days, that cannot be: on every day she did not jump, she did not see blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exactly רב הונא's וסת is based on. It rules out the first option, a cycle of days alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cycle of days would mean she bleeds on certain dates no matter what. Here the bleeding clearly depended on the jumping, so dates alone cannot be the pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? What is this about?
If you say
For days: a pattern based on dates

phrases.english: For what did she set it?
If you say for days,
but every day that she did not jump
she did not see blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רב הונא's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב הונא's וסת based on days or on jumps?

steps.title: Rather, the cycle is one of jumps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the וסת must be based on jumps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, she set a cycle for jumps.
steps.whatsHappening: Since days alone do not work, the גמרא suggests the pattern is that jumping brings on her bleeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This means that whenever she jumps, she should expect to see blood. This suggestion is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Jumps

phrases.english: Rather, for jumps,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with the second option
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The וסת is based on jumping.

steps.title: A ברייתא says an אונס pattern sets no וסת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this from a ברייתא. A pattern caused by אונס, even many times, does not set a וסת. That seems to mean no וסת at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: Any woman who sets a pattern because of an outside cause, even many times, has not set a וסת. Doesn't that mean no וסת at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea of a jumping cycle. A ברייתא says a pattern caused by an outside force never creates a וסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Jumping is a clear example of אונס. If the ברייתא means no וסת of any kind, then רב הונא's ruling seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of an outside cause
Doesn't it mean…? This pushes a reading.
At all

phrases.english: But it was taught in a ברייתא:
Any woman who sets it because of an outside cause,
even many times,
has not set a fixed cycle!

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לַָאו — לֹא קָבְעָה וֶסֶת כְּלָל?
phrases.english: Doesn't that mean she did not set a cycle at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'cycle of jumps' answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that jumping three times sets a וסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says an אונס pattern never sets a וסת. Jumping is אונס, so it should not set one.

steps.title: No: Only days alone or jumps alone fail; days plus jumps works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא narrowly. It rejects a cycle of days alone or jumps alone, but a combined cycle of days and jumps is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. She did not set a cycle for days alone or for jumps alone. But she did set a cycle for days and jumps together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא. It only rules out single-factor patterns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's case is a combined pattern: jumping on a particular day brings blood. The ברייתא does not argue with that kind of וסת, so רב הונא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: By themselves; alone
For days and jumps together

steps.whatToRemember: An אונס pattern alone sets no וסת. Days plus jumping together can set a וסת.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the ברייתא as saying אונס never matters. It only says a single factor alone is not enough.

phrases.english: No,
she did not set a cycle for days alone
or for jumps alone,
but she did set herself a cycle
for days and jumps together.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לֹא קָבְעָה וֶסֶת לְיָמִים לְחוֹדַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means an אונס pattern never sets any וסת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא rejects only days alone or jumps alone. A combined pattern of days and jumps is a valid וסת.

steps.title: Days alone is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say a cycle of days alone does not count. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That she sets no cycle for days alone is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. Why teach something obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood came only after jumping, nobody would think the dates alone caused it. So saying 'not days alone' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. This asks why something needed to be taught.

phrases.english: For days alone, it is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges part of the previous answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling, as just explained, that days alone do not set a וסת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When every sighting came after a jump, a cycle of days alone is clearly not possible, so why say it?

steps.title: רב אשי: A case where days alone might have seemed to count
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a case where a days-only cycle looks real. She jumped and saw on two Sundays. Then she jumped on Shabbat and saw nothing, and saw on Sunday without jumping.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: For example, she jumped on Sunday and saw, jumped on Sunday and saw, then on Shabbat she jumped and did not see, and on Sunday she saw without jumping.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the ruling about days alone is needed. He describes a case where it really looks like a Sunday cycle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She saw blood on three Sundays, and the third time without jumping. So one might think she has a Sunday cycle. The ruling teaches that this is not a cycle of days alone, since the third Sunday's blood can be credited to the jump the day before.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; in a case like
The first day of the week, Sunday
Without a jump

steps.whatToRemember: Even three Sundays of bleeding do not make a cycle of days alone when jumping was involved.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
For example, where she jumped on Sunday and saw blood,
and jumped on Sunday and saw blood,
and on Shabbat she jumped and did not see blood,
and on Sunday she saw blood without jumping.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי כְּגוֹן דִּקְפִיץ בְּחַד בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a specific case where the ruling is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Three Sunday sightings, one without jumping, might set a cycle of days alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even then it is not a cycle of days alone. The ruling is needed for this kind of case.

steps.title: The jump on Shabbat also caused the Sunday bleeding
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי finishes his answer. One might think his case proves the day alone caused the bleeding. The ברייתא teaches that the jump from the day before was also a cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: it now turns out, looking back, that the day (Sunday) is what causes her bleeding, not the jumping. So the ברייתא teaches us that yesterday's jump also caused it. She did not see blood on Shabbat only because the time for the jump to take effect had not yet come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains why the ברייתא had to tell us that a days-only pattern does not count. In his case it really looks like Sunday is the cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the third round she saw on Sunday without jumping that day, so it looks like the day alone is the trigger. The ברייתא says no: Saturday's jump also played a part, and its effect simply showed up a day later. So this is a combined pattern of days and jumps, not days alone.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces a mistaken assumption the text wants to correct)
It became clear looking back
It teaches us (the real lesson)
The time when the jump takes effect and causes bleeding

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רב אשי's case is a combined וסת of days and jumps: the Shabbat jump caused the Sunday bleeding.

phrases.english: You might have said:
the matter has been revealed, looking back,
that it is the day that causes it, and not the jumping,
phrases.notes: "The day" means Sunday, the day she kept seeing blood.

phrases.english: so it teaches us
that yesterday's jump also caused it,
and the fact that she did not see blood

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא מְטָא זְמַן קְפִיצָה.
phrases.english: is because the time for the jump to take effect had not yet arrived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's answer from step 9 by spelling out the mistaken thought and the correct lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is not obvious by giving a case where the mistaken reading looks likely
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since she saw on Sunday without jumping that day, the day alone is the cause, so it is a days-only וסת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Shabbat jump caused the Sunday bleeding with a delay, so it is a combined וסת of days and jumps.

steps.title: Second version: רב הונא says the pattern is for days, not jumps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another version of רב הונא's statement. If she jumped and saw three times, she sets a וסת for days and not for jumps.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: רב הונא said: If she jumped and saw, jumped and saw, jumped and saw, she has set a וסת for days, and not for jumps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts over with a different report of what רב הונא said. In this report, the jumps do not set the וסת. The days do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, jumping was part of the וסת. Here רב הונא says the jumping does not count. Only the pattern of days counts. The גמרא will next explain what case he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same statement
She has set a fixed cycle
A cycle based on days
Jumps

phrases.english: Another version:
Rav Huna said:
She jumped and saw blood, she jumped and saw blood,
she jumped and saw blood —
she has set herself a fixed cycle for days
and not for jumps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the whole first version with a different report of רב הונא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three times jumping and seeing sets a וסת for days, not for jumps.

steps.title: What case is רב הונא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact case where jumping and seeing would set a days-only וסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation רב הונא means. This sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It sounds strange that jumping each time would not count at all. So the גמרא needs a case where it becomes clear that the day, not the jump, is the real cause.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the case behind רב הונא's second version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The case where jumping and seeing leads to a days-only וסת.

steps.title: רב אשי: the same case now shows the day is the cause
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives the same case as before: two Sundays of jumping and seeing, then a jump on Shabbat with no blood, then blood on Sunday with no jump. In this version, that shows the day is the cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: She jumped on Sunday and saw, jumped on Sunday and saw, then on Shabbat she jumped and did not see, and on the next Sunday she saw without jumping. There it became clear that the day is what causes it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains רב הונא's case. Because she saw on Sunday even without jumping, we learn the day is the real cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact same case רב אשי used in the first version. There, we said the Shabbat jump caused the Sunday bleeding. Here we say the opposite: seeing without a jump proves Sunday itself is the trigger, so it is a וסת for days only.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunday (literally, the first day after Shabbat)
Without jumping
Causes

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Same case, opposite results: in the first version it is a combined days-and-jumps וסת; in this version it is a days-only וסת. Also, חד בשבת means Sunday, not Shabbat.
steps.whyThisMatters: The two versions disagree on whether a jump can cause bleeding a day later. That decides what kind of וסת she has.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is where she jumped on Sunday and saw blood,
and jumped on Sunday and saw blood,
and on Shabbat she jumped and did not see blood,
and on the next Sunday she saw blood without jumping,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets ("another") and some leave it out. Either way, it means the following Sunday.

phrases.english: for there the matter has been revealed
that it is the day that causes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: דִּקְפִיץ בְּחַד בְּשַׁבָּת וַחֲזַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 with the same case used in step 9, now read the other way.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of two Sundays with jumping, a Shabbat jump without blood, and Sunday blood without a jump. This shows Sunday is the cause.
steps.whatToRemember: Second version: seeing on Sunday without a jump proves the day is the cause, so the וסת is for days, not jumps.

steps.title: New משנה: even with a fixed cycle, she must check herself
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a woman with a fixed וסת must still check herself, except a נדה and a woman in her days of דם טוהר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Even though they said that for her, her time is enough, she still needs to check herself. This does not apply to a נדה or to a woman sitting in her days of דם טוהר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that a woman with a fixed וסת, even though she is not impure going backward, still has to check herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said that a woman with a fixed וסת is impure only from the time she sees, not backward (דיה שעתה). This משנה adds that she must still check herself. The exceptions are women whose status is already known: a נדה is already impure, and a woman in her days of דם טוהר is pure even if she bleeds.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה (start of a new משנה)
Her time is enough: she is impure only from the time she sees, not backward
Checks herself
A woman in her state of menstrual impurity
Blood of purity: the days after birth when bleeding does not make her impure

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ,
phrases.english: Even though they said, "her time is enough,"
she still needs to be checking herself,
except for the נדה
and the woman sitting in her days of blood of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ דַּיָּהּ שְׁעָתָהּ, צְרִיכָה לִהְיוֹת בּוֹדֶקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of jumping ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman with a fixed וסת must still check herself, except a נדה and a woman in her days of דם טוהר.

steps.title: She uses checking cloths at relations, with two exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that she uses checking cloths when she is with her husband, except a woman in her days of דם טוהר and a בתולה whose blood is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she uses checking cloths when she is with her husband, except for a woman sitting in her days of דם טוהר, and a בתולה whose blood is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule: she must use cloths to check at relations. Two women do not need to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking cloths show if her flow started during relations. A woman in her days of דם טוהר does not need them because any blood is pure anyway. A בתולה whose bleeding comes from the first relations also does not need them, since that blood is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Is with her husband (has relations)
Checking cloths (here, not witnesses)
A בתולה whose blood is pure (blood from first relations)

steps.confusionAlert: Here עדים means checking cloths, not witnesses in court.
steps.whatToRemember: A fixed וסת does not free a woman from checking. She checks daily and uses cloths at relations, except where her status is already clear.

phrases.english: And she is with her husband using checking cloths,
phrases.notes: Literally "witnesses"; the cloths "testify" whether blood appeared.

phrases.english: except for the woman sitting in her days of blood of purity,
and a virgin whose blood is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second checking rule to the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She uses checking cloths at relations, except a woman in her days of דם טוהר and a בתולה whose blood is pure.

steps.title: The regular times a woman checks herself
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the regular checking times: morning, twilight, and before being with her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: She needs to check herself twice a day, in the morning and at twilight, and also when she is about to be with her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues from Steps 14-15 and tells us when a woman checks herself: twice a day, plus before being with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The morning check covers the night, and the twilight check covers the day. The check before being with her husband makes sure she is טהורה at that exact time.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking herself to see whether there is blood
Morning
Twilight, between sunset and nightfall
A polite phrase for being with her husband

phrases.english: And twice she needs to be checking herself:
in the morning, and at twilight,
and at the time that she is about
to be with her husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rules about checking from Steps 14-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman checks in the morning, at twilight, and before being with her husband.

steps.title: Women of כהנים families check more often
steps.stepSummary: Women from כהנים families also check before eating תרומה. רבי יהודה adds that they check after eating it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women of כהנים families have extra checks beyond these: when they eat תרומה. רבי יהודה says: also when they finish eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds extra checking times for women who eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה must be eaten in טהרה, so she checks before eating to be sure she is טהורה. רבי יהודה adds a check after eating, to know whether she saw blood while she was eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Women of כהנים families, who may eat תרומה
The holy portion of produce given to a כהן, eaten only in טהרה
They have more than them, meaning extra obligations

phrases.english: Women of priestly families have more checks than them,
at the time that they eat teruma.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Also at the time they finish
eating teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds extra checking times for כהנות on top of the regular times in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנות also check when eating תרומה. רבי יהודה adds that they check when they finish eating it.

steps.title: Why a נדה does not need to check
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה's exception: during her days of נדה, she does not need to check.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Except a נדה": because during her days of נדה, she does not need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes the exception from the משנה and gives a simple reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is already טמאה during these days, so a check would not change anything. This simple explanation sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A woman who is טמאה because of her period
Her days of נדה, the days she is טמאה from her period

phrases.english: Gemara:
"Except for a niddah."
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה from Step 14.

phrases.english: Because within the days of her niddah
she does not need checking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by explaining the exception of נדה from Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During her days of נדה, a woman does not need to check.

steps.title: According to רבי יוחנן, she should check
steps.stepSummary: This fits ריש לקיש, who holds that no וסת is set during days of נדה. But רבי יוחנן holds that a וסת can be set then, so she should check.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who says a woman can set a וסת during her days of זיבה but not during her days of נדה. But according to רבי יוחנן, who says a woman can set a וסת during her days of נדה, she should check, because maybe she is setting a וסת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from Step 18. It says the explanation only fits one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no וסת can be set during days of נדה, checking then has no purpose, so ריש לקיש is fine. But רבי יוחנן says a וסת can be set then. So she should check, to know whether a pattern is forming.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well for, the opening of a challenge from one opinion
She sets a fixed pattern for her period
Her days of זיבה, when blood makes her a זבה
Maybe

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ימי נדה and ימי זיבה. They are two different sets of days, and ריש לקיש treats them differently.

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish,
who said: A woman can set a fixed cycle for herself
within the days of her zivah,
but a woman does not set a fixed cycle for herself
within the days of her niddah. That is fine.
phrases.notes: For him, blood during the days of נדה is just part of the same period, so no pattern can form.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said:
A woman can set a fixed cycle for herself
within the days of her niddah,
let her check, because maybe she is setting a fixed cycle!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that a נדה does not need to check during her days of נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן holds that a וסת can be set during days of נדה. If so, she should check, to know whether a וסת is forming.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits his rule to a closed source
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that a וסת is set during days of נדה only when the blood starts fresh, not when it comes while she is already flowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן could tell you: When I said it, I meant where she saw blood from a closed source. But if she saw it from an open source, I did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge for רבי יוחנן. It narrows what he meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A וסת counts only from blood that starts fresh, after the source was closed. Blood that comes in the middle of a flow does not start a pattern. So during her days of נדה, checking would not help her set a וסת, and the משנה's exception works even for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: A closed source: bleeding that starts fresh
An open source: bleeding that comes while she is already flowing
When I said it, used to limit what one meant

steps.whatToRemember: Even רבי יוחנן agrees that blood seen while the source is already open does not start a וסת. That is why a נדה does not need to check.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan could say to you:
When I said it,
I meant where she saw it from a closed source,
phrases.notes: He means the bleeding began fresh, at the start of a period.

phrases.english: but if she saw it from an open source,
phrases.notes: He means the bleeding came in the middle of a period that had already started.

phrases.english: I did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by narrowing רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seemed to say that any blood during days of נדה can set a וסת, so she should check.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only blood from a closed source sets a וסת. Blood from an open source does not, so checking during days of נדה is not needed.

steps.title: First reading of 'sitting on דם טוהר'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's second exception and first assumes it means a woman about to begin her days of דם טוהר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that a woman 'sitting on דם טוהר' does not need to check. At first you might think this means a woman who is just about to start her days of דם טוהר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next exception in the משנה and offers a first understanding of it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After birth, a woman has a set of impure days, followed by days of דם טוהר, when blood she sees is pure. The first reading is that the משנה is talking about the moment she switches from the impure days to the pure days. So the משנה would be saying she does not need to check at the end of her impure days.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood of purity: blood a woman sees during the set days after birth, which the תורה treats as pure
It might enter your mind: a first assumption that may be changed later
About to begin sitting: she is just starting this period

steps.confusionAlert: The words קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ tell you this is only a first guess. Do not treat this reading as the final meaning of the משנה.

phrases.english: "And the woman who sits on the blood of purity"
it enters your mind (at first you might think)
that it means one who is about to begin sitting on the blood of purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיּוֹשֶׁבֶת עַל דַּם טוֹהַר, קָא סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the נדה exception (steps 18-20) to the משנה's second exception, the woman sitting on דם טוהר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First assumption: the משנה exempts a woman who is about to move from her impure days after birth into her days of דם טוהר from checking.

steps.title: This reading works for רב but not for לוי
steps.stepSummary: If blood after birth comes from one source, there is no need to check. But if there are two sources, she should check that the impure one has stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רב, who says it is one source: the תורה made it impure and the תורה made it pure. That is fine. But for לוי, who says there are two sources, she should check. Maybe that impure source has not stopped yet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first reading against a disagreement between רב and לוי. It shows that the reading fits רב but causes a problem for לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the same source flows the whole time. Only the day decides if the blood is pure or impure, so once her pure days begin, any blood is pure and checking adds nothing. For לוי, there are two separate sources, so blood seen on the first pure day might still be from the impure source. That means she should have to check.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well: the view fits one opinion before the challenge to the other
Source (literally 'spring'): where the blood comes from in the body
Fine, well: no problem
Still, yet

steps.whyThisMatters: The argument between רב and לוי decides whether the change from impure to pure depends only on the calendar or on which source the blood actually comes from.

phrases.english: This works well according to רב, who said:
It is one source,
the תורה made it impure, and the תורה made it pure
phrases.notes: The same blood is impure in the first days after birth and pure in the later days. Only the time is different.

phrases.english: it is fine.
But according to לוי, who said:
They are two sources,
she should check,

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא אַכַּתִּי לָא פְּסַק הָהוּא מַעְיָן טָמֵא!
phrases.english: perhaps that impure source has still not stopped!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַב, דְּאָמַר: מַעְיָן אֶחָד הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first reading from step 21 using לוי's view of two sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first reading of the משנה, that a woman about to begin her days of דם טוהר does not need to check
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to לוי, the impure and pure blood come from different sources. So at the switch-over, blood might still be coming from the impure source, and checking would be needed. The משנה's exemption therefore seems not to fit לוי.

steps.title: לוי asks whose opinion the משנה follows
steps.stepSummary: לוי begins his defense by asking which תנא this משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי could answer you: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: לוי starts his answer by asking which sage the משנה follows. This sets up the rest of his answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the משנה his own way, לוי is about to say the משנה follows a particular תנא whose view differs from his. This would show that the משנה is not a problem for לוי's own position.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose is this? A question asking which sage a ruling follows

phrases.english: לוי could say to you:
Whose opinion is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins לוי's answer to the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא (the answer continues in the next lines)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to state a rule for everyone, which would contradict לוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי will say the משנה follows one particular תנא, so it does not have to match his own view.
